history.hpi: Mother reports patient has had a cold for two days and started wheezing badly this morning. Rescue inhaler used six times in the last two hours without relief. Patient now sitting bolt upright, unable to speak more than one or two words at a time, visibly exhausted.
pastMedical: Asthma, prior PICU admission at age 10 for status asthmaticus
history.events: Mother called 911 after rescue inhaler stopped helping and patient became too breathless to talk

scene.location: Single-family home, patient's bedroom, sitting upright on edge of bed
scene.bystanders: Mother present, anxious, holding patient's empty rescue inhaler
visualCues: Patient tripoding, using every accessory muscle to breathe
Nebulizer and empty MDI canister on nightstand
Patient mouthing words rather than speaking, unable to complete a sentence

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew finds a 14-year-old female in severe respiratory distress, tripoding, with minimal audible air movement and suprasternal retractions. She is exhausted and can only mouth single words.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent but severely compromised air movement
clinicalPresentation.breathing: Severe accessory muscle use, suprasternal and intercostal retractions, minimal air movement bilaterally on auscultation
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses rapid and thready, skin pale and diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Intact but patient too exhausted to sit unsupported
otherFindings: Unable to speak more than one word at a time
Wheezing quiet/almost absent — minimal air movement, not clear breath sounds
Visible fatigue, tripod positioning
Peak inspiratory effort with little chest rise

transitions.if: Impending respiratory failure recognized, epi/mag given
transitions.condition: Crew recognizes the near-silent chest and minimal air movement as impending respiratory failure and escalates immediately to IM epinephrine and IV magnesium alongside continuous nebulized bronchodilators, rather than waiting on standard nebulizer treatment alone.

phases.name: Impending respiratory failure recognized, epi/mag given
phases.description: Crew recognizes minimal air movement and accessory muscle use as signs of impending respiratory failure. Continuous nebulized albuterol/ipratropium is started, IM epinephrine is given as adjunctive therapy, IV access is obtained, and magnesium sulfate is infused.
phases.triggerCondition: The near-absent wheeze ("quiet chest") combined with severe accessory muscle use and patient exhaustion meets the protocol's threshold for impending respiratory failure, prompting escalation beyond standard nebulizer therapy to IM epinephrine and IV magnesium.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Continued retractions but slightly more audible air movement after nebulizer/epi
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses rapid, skin pale and diaphoretic
otherFindings: Continuous albuterol/ipratropium nebulizer running
IM epinephrine administered to anterolateral thigh
IV established, magnesium sulfate infusing over 10-15 minutes
Waveform capnography placed showing shark-fin morphology

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize impending respiratory failure: near-silent chest, minimal air movement, exhaustion
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Signs of distress include: Apprehension, anxiety, combativeness. Hypoxia (less than 90% oxygen saturation). Intercostal/subcostal/supraclavicular retractions, accessory muscle use. In the setting of severe bronchoconstriction, wheezing may not be heard. Patients with known asthma with severe dyspnea should be empirically treated, even if wheezing is absent
expectedActions.rationale: A quiet chest in a known asthmatic is a pre-arrest finding, not reassurance of mild disease.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

expectedActions.shortAction: Continuous nebulized albuterol 5 mg with ipratropium 0.5 mg (up to 3 doses)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Albuterol 5 mg nebulized (or 6 puffs metered dose inhaler) should be administered to all patients in respiratory distress with signs of bronchospasm (e.g., known asthmatics, quiet wheezers). Repeat at this dose with unlimited frequency for ongoing respiratory distress. Ipratropium 0.5 mg nebulized should be given up to 3 doses in conjunction with albuterol
expectedActions.rationale: Repeated bronchodilator dosing is indicated for ongoing distress regardless of frequency limits.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

expectedActions.shortAction: Epinephrine 0.3 mg IM 1 mg/mL (50 kg × 0.01 mg/kg = 0.5 mg → capped at 0.3 mg max)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Epinephrine (0.01 mg/kg of 1 mg/mL solution IM, maximum dose of 0.3 mg) should only be administered for impending respiratory failure as adjunctive therapy when there are no clinical signs of improvement with the above treatments
expectedActions.rationale: IM epinephrine is reserved for impending respiratory failure, exactly this presentation.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

expectedActions.shortAction: Magnesium sulfate 2 g IV (50 kg × 40 mg/kg = 2000 mg = 2 g; max dose 2 g) over 10-15 min
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Magnesium sulfate (40 mg/kg IV, maximum dose of 2 g) over 10–15 minutes should be administered for severe bronchoconstriction and concern for impending respiratory failure
expectedActions.rationale: This patient's weight-based dose lands exactly at the protocol maximum.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

expectedActions.shortAction: Place continuous waveform capnography to monitor severe bronchospasm and guide therapy
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Continuous waveform capnography monitoring should be placed in line. Continuous waveform capnography...should be used in spontaneously breathing patients who are...in severe respiratory distress (e.g., receiving epinephrine, magnesium therapy)
expectedActions.rationale: A shark-fin waveform confirms ongoing severe obstructive physiology and tracks response to treatment.

transitions.if: NIV started early, air movement improves
transitions.condition: Non-invasive ventilation (CPAP with nebulizer in-line via T-connector) is started promptly alongside continued bronchodilator/epi/magnesium therapy, and the patient's air movement and mental status improve, avoiding the need for invasive airway management.
Crew continues only standard nebulizer treatment without escalating to NIV or reassessing frequently; the patient's silent chest and exhaustion progress unrecognized to frank respiratory arrest.

phases.name: NIV started early, air movement improves
phases.description: CPAP is applied early with continuous nebulized bronchodilator delivered in-line through a T-connector. The patient's air movement, mental status, and vital signs steadily improve without requiring invasive airway management.
phases.triggerCondition: Early initiation of non-invasive ventilation with nebulizer in-line, combined with ongoing epinephrine and magnesium therapy, reverses the impending respiratory failure trajectory before it progresses to arrest.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Improved air movement bilaterally, decreased accessory muscle use, tolerating CPAP
otherFindings: CPAP mask seal maintained continuously
Nebulizer running in-line via T-connector
Patient able to speak in short phrases again
Waveform capnography shows improving shark-fin morphology
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I can breathe a little easier now."

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply CPAP with nebulizer in-line via T-connector; maintain continuous mask seal
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) should be considered early for severe respiratory distress or impending respiratory failure. Nebulized medications may be administered through a CPAP or BiPAP mask. A specialized T-connector with a spring valve assembly is required to allow maintenance of positive airway pressure
expectedActions.rationale: Early NIV can avert the need for invasive airway management in severe bronchospasm.

expectedActions.shortAction: Do not break CPAP mask seal until hospital CPAP is ready to take over
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Once initiated and patient is tolerating mask, DO NOT discontinue CPAP/BiPAP until patient is on the emergency department stretcher and hospital CPAP/BiPAP is immediately available for patient to be switched over...Breaking the mask seal causes a significant decrease in airway pressures and may lead to abrupt decompensation due to atelectasis and alveolar collapse
expectedActions.rationale: Interrupting CPAP to reposition the patient or during transfer can trigger rapid decompensation.

phases.name: Escalation delayed despite silent chest
phases.description: Without escalation to NIV, the patient's exhaustion progresses to frank respiratory arrest. Crew initiates two-person BVM ventilation with PEEP at a pediatric rate while preparing for advanced airway management.
phases.triggerCondition: Continued reliance on standard nebulizer treatment without reassessing for escalation allows the silent chest and exhaustion to progress unrecognized to apnea and respiratory arrest.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: No spontaneous effort; two-person BVM with PEEP delivering ventilations
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Pulses weak and slow, cyanosis developing
otherFindings: Two-person, two-thumbs-up BVM technique in use
PEEP valve set at 5 cmH2O initial
Ventilating at pediatric rate given patient age
Preparing RSI equipment

expectedActions.shortAction: Two-person BVM with PEEP 5 cmH2O at pediatric rate 20-30/min
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Use bag-valve-mask (BVM) ventilation in the setting of respiratory failure or arrest...Two-person, two-thumbs-up BVM ventilation is preferred. PEEP should be used with BVM...5 cmH2O is generally an appropriate initial PEEP setting. Rate: Child: 20–30 breaths/minute
expectedActions.rationale: This 14-year-old patient falls under the protocol's pediatric ventilation rate, not the adult 10-12/min rate.

transitions.condition: BVM ventilation fails to achieve adequate oxygenation and ventilation despite PEEP and airway adjuncts, and the crew proceeds to rapid sequence intubation with pediatric tube sizing.

phases.name: BVM ineffective, RSI performed
phases.description: BVM ventilation is inadequate to overcome the severe bronchospasm, and the crew proceeds to rapid sequence intubation using pediatric tube sizing and ketamine for its bronchodilatory properties, then confirms placement and begins controlled ventilation.
phases.triggerCondition: Persistent hypoxia and inadequate ventilation despite optimized BVM technique meet the protocol's threshold for advanced airway management via RSI.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Secured with endotracheal tube, placement confirmed
clinicalPresentation.breathing: Controlled ventilation via BVM/ventilator, bilateral breath sounds present
otherFindings: Pediatric-sized cuffed endotracheal tube placed (age/4 + 3.5 = 7.0 mm)
Placement confirmed via waveform capnography, bilateral breath sounds, absent gastric sounds
Tube secured and depth documented
Ketamine chosen for induction given bronchodilatory effect

expectedActions.shortAction: RSI with ketamine 75 mg IV (50 kg × 1.5 mg/kg) then rocuronium 50 mg IV (50 kg × 1 mg/kg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer induction sedative agent: Ketamine IV push, 1-2 mg/kg...Administer paralytic agent: Rocuronium IV push, 1 mg/kg
expectedActions.rationale: Ketamine's bronchodilatory effect makes it the preferred induction agent in severe bronchospasm.

expectedActions.shortAction: Size endotracheal tube using pediatric formula: (14/4) + 3.5 = 7.0 mm cuffed
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: For pediatrics, cuffed tubes are now recommended...2–15 years: [age(yrs.)/4]+4 (uncuffed) or [age(yrs.)/4]+3.5 (cuffed)
expectedActions.rationale: At 14 years old this patient still falls under pediatric tube-sizing formulas rather than the fixed adult 7.5/8.0 sizes.

expectedActions.shortAction: Confirm tube placement with waveform capnography, bilateral breath sounds, absent gastric sounds
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Confirm placement of advanced airway (endotracheal tube, SGA) with waveform capnography (most reliable), absent gastric sounds, and bilateral breath sounds
expectedActions.rationale: Capnography is the most reliable confirmation method and must be verified before securing the tube.
